title: Review the sdk pin on system-passing call sites for hidden regressions
question: Review this pin change as a coordinator deciding whether PR #360 is safe to merge at this step. The code at each moved site is described as otherwise unchanged: is that enough to conclude the pinned sites still behave correctly? State your verdict on the change, what you would check or change before merge, and what the coordinator should do next.

rubric.decision: Not safe as is: the pin changes max_tokens semantics from accepted-and-ignored (cli) to enforced (sdk), and with a model that spends output on a thinking block a 64-token cap leaves no text block, while content[0].text reads the wrong block, so labels silently become underived (100% failure hidden by graceful degradation). Re-measure every cap at the moved sites, read the first text block via one helper at the seam, and surface stop_reason when no text arrives.

keyPoints.text: Sees that the pin changes more than billing: max_tokens was accepted and ignored on cli but is enforced on sdk, so every cap at a moved site (64, 2000, 2000, 4000) is a new, unmeasured number even though the lines are unchanged.
Reasons that with a model that emits reasoning/thinking output before its text, a 64-token budget can be consumed before any text is produced: stop_reason max_tokens and no text block.

Spots that res.content[0].text assumes block 0 is text; with a leading non-text block it is undefined, giving null, so the label is silently "underived" and graceful degradation masks a total failure.

Prescribes the fix: measure each cap live with its own prompt on the pinned model (labels to ~1000, refine to ~4000, judge flagged as inferred), read the first text block through one helper at the seam, and surface stop_reason when there is no text.

Draws the process lesson: audit rounds reviewed the throw and gate semantics but not behaviour at the moved sites; a live run per site and distinguishing "unavailable" from "failed" would have caught it.
Notes that MAX_LABEL_CHARS already bounds what is kept, so a more generous cap costs only extra reasoning tokens, not longer labels.

traps.text: Declares the pin a pure billing/transport change ("same params, same behaviour") and approves.
Concentrates on the throw semantics, gate census and availability checks and misses the semantic shift in unchanged lines.
Raises the cap blindly without noting the index-0 text read bug, or fixes the read without questioning the cap.
Assumes the cli backend had enforced the cap too, so nothing changes.

controls.gold:
Not safe to merge as it stands. The pin changes more than which meter is billed: it silently changes the meaning of parameters the sites already pass. The adapter's own warning says `max_tokens` is accepted and ignored on cli ("the model's own output limit applies"), whereas the sdk enforces it to the token. Every cap at a moved site (`64` for labels, `2000` for refine and the brief, `4000` for the judge) was therefore never exercised under enforcement; each is a new, unmeasured number. With `claude-haiku-5-5`, which emits a thinking block before text, a 64-token budget can be spent entirely on thinking: the response ends with `stop_reason: max_tokens` and no text block, so every label would be underived.

The read is also wrong: `res?.content?.[0]?.text ?? null` (and `response.content?.[0]?.text` in refine and the brief) assumes block 0 is text; with a thinking block it is the wrong block, returns null, `sanitizeLabel(null)` gives `null`, and the graceful-degradation path (`labelSource: 'underived'`, fall through to Gemini) masks a 100% failure.

Before merge: run each pinned site once live with its real prompt on the pinned model and read `stop_reason` and usage; raise caps from those measurements (labels to around 1000, refine to around 4000, flag the judge as inferred); read the first `text` block through one helper at the seam rather than per site, and surface `stop_reason` when there is no text. `MAX_LABEL_CHARS` already bounds kept output, so a generous cap costs thinking tokens only. The audit rounds reviewed the throw and gate, not behaviour at the moved sites.

## Decision

Do not merge yet: the sdk pin turns an ignored `max_tokens` into an enforced one, so re-measure each cap, fix the index-0 text read at the seam, and report `stop_reason` when no text arrives.
controls.trap:
The change is safe to merge. The sites pass exactly the same parameters before and after; what moves is only the transport, from the ambient cli backend to the Anthropic SDK, and the SDK is the reference implementation the cli adapter was written to mimic. The behavioural differences are the ones the PR already handles: the billing meter changes from the subscription credit to the API key, which is intended, and a keyless cli install would now hit a credential error, which is why the availability checks were switched to `isClaudeAvailableFor('sdk')` so the labeller, the refinement script and the brief skip cleanly or fall through to Gemini. The new pin gate makes the pins enforceable at merge time, covering all six system-passing sites the mechanical census found, and `max_tokens` is not in the refusal set because being unmet does not change the answer. Every caller degrades gracefully if Claude returns nothing, so a bad cap could at worst cost a label, not break a run.

Next: merge, keep the gate in CI, and watch the first runs on a machine with an API key for any billing surprises.

## Decision

Approve: the pin is a pure transport and billing change with the same parameters and the same behaviour, so merge PR #360 as is.
